h2. 2. Problem Statement

h3. 2.1 Current State

Administrators managing Red Hat OpenStack Platform today rely on Heat templates, Ansible playbooks, or direct OpenStack API/CLI calls to provision and lifecycle-manage infrastructure resources. These approaches are imperative, difficult to reconcile against desired state, and do not integrate natively with Kubernetes-based GitOps workflows that many organizations are adopting.

The upstream ORC project ({{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}}) exists and is actively developed — it has reached v2.5.0 as of April 2026, with 24 implemented controllers spanning Neutron, Nova, Glance, Cinder, and Keystone. It is already consumed in production by Cluster API Provider OpenStack (CAPO). However, it is not productized by Red Hat, has no customer-facing support boundary, and is not shipped as part of any RHOSP release.

h3. 2.2 Desired State

Red Hat ships a Tech Preview of ORC as part of its OpenStack product offering. Customers who use Kubernetes as a control plane can declare OpenStack infrastructure resources as Kubernetes objects, have them continuously reconciled, and integrate OpenStack provisioning into existing GitOps pipelines (ArgoCD, Flux). The Tech Preview clearly communicates which controllers are ready for evaluation and which remain experimental.

h3. 2.3 Business Impact

* Enables RHOSP customers to adopt cloud-native, declarative infrastructure management without abandoning their OpenStack investment.
* Aligns with the CAPO strategic direction, where ORC is already the resource management dependency layer in production.
* Reduces configuration drift incidents by enabling continuous desired-state reconciliation.
* Provides a differentiated capability not currently offered by competitors at a productized level.

----

h2. 3. Goals & Objectives

h3. Primary Goals

* Package and ship ORC as a Tech Preview feature accessible to RHOSP customers.
* Define the subset of the 24 upstream controllers mature enough for Tech Preview inclusion and explicitly exclude those that are not.
* Communicate the maturity status of each included controller clearly in documentation.
* Establish a Tech Preview support boundary (community-level, best-effort) and ensure customers understand it.
* Provide installation, configuration, and usage documentation sufficient for non-production evaluation.

h3. Success Metrics

||Metric||Current||Target||Measurement Method||
|Controllers included in Tech Preview|0 (not productized)|≥ 8 controllers based on upstream maturity assessment|Controller maturity review at ship time|
|Customer adoption|0|≥ 5 customer environments within 90 days of Tech Preview ship|Telemetry / customer success reports|
|P1 bugs in included controllers at ship|Unknown|0|Bug tracker at release|
|Documentation completeness|0%|100% of included controllers documented with examples|Doc review gate|
|Time to first reconciled resource (new install)|N/A|≤ 30 minutes following documented install steps|QE validation|

----

h2. 4. User Personas

h3. Persona 1: OpenStack Platform Administrator

* *Role*: Infrastructure engineer or cloud administrator managing a RHOSP environment.
* *Goals*: Provision and lifecycle-manage OpenStack resources (networks, subnets, routers, security groups, images, flavors) in a repeatable, auditable, declarative manner — without writing Heat templates or imperative scripts.
* *Pain Points*: Current tooling (Heat, Ansible, CLI) does not integrate with GitOps workflows; configuration drift is hard to detect and remediate; there is no continuous reconciliation of declared vs. actual state.
* *Usage Context*: Uses a Kubernetes cluster as a control plane alongside an existing RHOSP deployment; wants to store OpenStack resource definitions in Git and have them automatically applied and reconciled.

h3. Persona 2: Platform Engineering / DevOps Engineer

* *Role*: Engineer responsible for integrating infrastructure provisioning into CI/CD and GitOps pipelines.
* *Goals*: Treat OpenStack infrastructure as code using Kubernetes-native manifests; integrate OpenStack provisioning into ArgoCD or Flux pipelines alongside application deployments.
* *Pain Points*: No Kubernetes-native way to manage OpenStack resources; forced to maintain separate tooling stacks (Terraform, Ansible) outside the GitOps control plane.
* *Usage Context*: Defines OpenStack CRs in a Git repository; a GitOps operator syncs them to a management Kubernetes cluster running ORC; ORC reconciles desired state against the OpenStack API.

----

h2. 5. Requirements

h3. 5.1 Functional Requirements

||ID||Requirement||Priority||Acceptance Criteria||
|FR-001|ORC must be installable on a supported Kubernetes/OpenShift cluster via a defined, documented method (server-side apply of a release manifest bundle).|MVP|Installation procedure documented; QE can complete installation in a clean environment following only the documentation.|
|FR-002|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Network* resources (create, update, delete, reconcile).|MVP|A Network CR can be applied; ORC creates the corresponding OpenStack network; deletion of the CR removes the network; existing networks can be imported by filter or by name.|
|FR-003|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Subnet* resources (create, update, delete, reconcile).|MVP|A Subnet CR can be applied referencing a Network CR; ORC creates the subnet in the correct network; cross-resource dependency ordering is enforced.|
|FR-004|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Router* resources and their subnet interface attachments via *RouterInterface* resources.|MVP|A Router CR can be applied; ORC creates the router; RouterInterface CRs attach subnets to the router in the correct order.|
|FR-005|ORC must support management of OpenStack *SecurityGroup* resources, including inline security group rules.|MVP|A SecurityGroup CR can be applied; ORC creates the security group and all specified rules; updates to rules are reconciled correctly.|
|FR-006|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Image* (Glance) resources including upload from a remote URL source.|MVP|An Image CR can be applied referencing an image source URL; ORC downloads and registers the image in Glance; image hash verification is performed if specified.|
|FR-007|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Flavor* resources (create, delete; immutable fields enforced).|MVP|A Flavor CR can be applied; ORC creates the Nova flavor; attempts to update immutable fields are reported as a terminal error, not silently ignored.|
|FR-008|ORC must support management of OpenStack *AddressScope* (Neutron) resources.|MVP|An AddressScope CR can be applied; ORC creates the address scope; deletion removes it from Neutron.|
|FR-009|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Trunk* (Neutron) resources.|MVP|A Trunk CR can be applied referencing a parent Port CR; ORC creates the trunk and sub-ports.|
|FR-010|ORC must expose standard Kubernetes status conditions on each CR ({{Progressing}}, {{Available}}) reflecting actual reconciliation state.|MVP|All CRs surface {{.status.conditions}}; {{Available=True}} is set when the resource is ready; error conditions include a human-readable message referencing the OpenStack API response.|
|FR-011|ORC must store the OpenStack UUID of each managed resource in {{.status.id}} after successful creation.|MVP|After a resource is created, {{.status.id}} contains the UUID; {{.status.resource}} reflects the full observed OpenStack state.|
|FR-012|ORC must support referencing OpenStack credentials via a Kubernetes Secret (containing a {{clouds.yaml}}) on each CR via a {{cloudCredentialsRef}} field.|MVP|A valid Secret is referenced; ORC authenticates using those credentials; an invalid or expired credential is reflected as a terminal error condition on the CR.|
|FR-013|ORC must support importing existing OpenStack resources into management without recreating them, using either a name/filter-based import or direct ID import.|MVP|A CR with {{spec.import}} referencing an existing OpenStack resource causes ORC to adopt that resource; no recreation occurs; filter matching more than one resource produces a terminal error.|
|FR-014|ORC must support a management policy field per CR that allows unmanaged mode (status-tracking only, no modification).|MVP|A CR with {{managementPolicy: unmanaged}} causes ORC to track and report resource status without modifying the OpenStack resource.|
|FR-015|ORC must handle transient OpenStack API errors with retry and exponential backoff; permanent errors must surface as terminal conditions without infinite crash-looping.|MVP|Transient errors (network timeouts) cause retry; 409 Neutron quota-exceeded errors are treated as retryable; non-retryable errors produce a terminal {{Available=False}} condition.|
|FR-016|The Tech Preview release must include documentation clearly identifying each included controller's maturity status (Tech Preview / Experimental / Not Included).|MVP|A maturity matrix is published with the Tech Preview; every controller is labeled; known limitations per controller are documented.|
|FR-017|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Port* (Neutron) resources.|Non-MVP|A Port CR can be applied referencing a Network and optionally a Subnet; ORC creates the Neutron port; IP addresses, port security, VNIC type, and {{valueSpecs}} are configurable.|
|FR-018|ORC must support management of OpenStack *FloatingIP* (Neutron) resources.|Non-MVP|A FloatingIP CR can be applied; ORC allocates a floating IP from a specified network and optionally associates it with a Port CR.|
|FR-019|ORC must support management of OpenStack *KeyPair* (Nova) resources.|Non-MVP|A KeyPair CR can be applied; ORC creates the keypair in Nova; the public key may be provided inline or referenced from a Secret.|
|FR-020|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Server* (Nova) resources.|Non-MVP|A Server CR can be applied specifying flavor, image, network interfaces, keypair, and availability zone; ORC creates the Nova instance; Server waits for dependent ORC resources to be Available before provisioning.|
|FR-021|ORC must support management of OpenStack *ServerGroup* (Nova) resources.|Non-MVP|A ServerGroup CR can be applied with a specified policy (e.g., anti-affinity, affinity, soft variants); ORC creates the server group; Server CRs can reference a ServerGroup CR.|
|FR-022|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Volume* (Cinder) resources, including creation of bootable volumes from images.|Non-MVP|A Volume CR can be applied specifying size, type, and optionally an image source; ORC creates the Cinder volume; availability zone is configurable.|
|FR-023|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Project* (Keystone) resources.|Non-MVP|A Project CR can be applied; ORC creates the Keystone project; {{domainRef}} is supported for domain-scoped projects.|

h3. 5.2 Non-Functional Requirements

||ID||Requirement||Category||Target||
|NFR-001|ORC must not modify or delete OpenStack resources it does not manage. Resources with no corresponding ORC CR must never be affected by ORC operations.|Safety|Zero unintended deletions of unmanaged resources during QE validation.|
|NFR-002|ORC must document that Tech Preview is not covered by Red Hat production support SLAs; this disclaimer must appear in all installation documentation and on the product page.|Supportability|Tech Preview disclaimer visible in all installation docs; QE review gate.|
|NFR-003|ORC reconciliation must complete a no-op pass (resource already in desired state) for non-image resources within 30 seconds under normal conditions.|Performance|Measured during QE validation on a representative environment.|
|NFR-004|ORC must enforce namespace-scoped operation: all cross-resource references (other ORC CRs, credential Secrets) must reside in the same namespace as the referencing CR.|Security|Cross-namespace references are rejected by admission validation; no cluster-admin privileges required for namespace-scoped operation.|
|NFR-005|ORC must log reconciliation events and errors in a structured format compatible with standard Kubernetes log aggregation; log level must be configurable; errors must include the resource name/namespace and the OpenStack request ID.|Observability|Logs are structured JSON or key=value; OpenStack {{Request-ID}} is surfaced in error logs (enabled via ReconcileID forwarding).|
|NFR-006|ORC must run on Kubernetes v1.29 or later (required for CEL validation support).|Compatibility|QE validates against the minimum supported OpenShift version at Tech Preview ship time; CEL validation is tested.|
|NFR-007|ORC must not expose OpenStack API credentials in Kubernetes event logs or status conditions.|Security|Credential values never appear in {{.status}}, events, or controller logs; only error summaries (not raw API responses containing credentials) are surfaced.|

----

h2. 6. User Stories

*US-001*: As an OpenStack Platform Administrator, I want to define Network, Subnet, and Router resources as Kubernetes manifests so that I can manage OpenStack network topology declaratively and store it in Git. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given a valid Network CR applied to the cluster, when ORC reconciles it, then the corresponding OpenStack network exists with the specified properties.   - Given a Subnet CR referencing that Network CR, when the Network CR is Available, then ORC creates the subnet in the correct network — without requiring manual ordering.   - Given the Network CR is deleted while a Subnet CR still references it, when ORC processes the deletion, then the Network deletion is blocked until the Subnet CR is removed first.   - Given the OpenStack network already exists with the desired properties, when ORC reconciles, then no changes are made and the CR status shows {{Available=True}}.

*US-002*: As a Platform Engineering / DevOps Engineer, I want ORC CRs to expose standard Kubernetes status conditions so that I can integrate OpenStack resource readiness into GitOps health checks and pipeline gates. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given a CR is successfully reconciled, then {{Available=True}} is set on the CR with a timestamp.   - Given a CR fails to reconcile due to an OpenStack API error, then the {{Available=False}} condition includes an actionable message and the OpenStack request ID for correlation.   - Given an ArgoCD Application monitors ORC CRs, when all CRs are {{Available=True}}, then ArgoCD reports the Application as Healthy.

*US-003*: As an OpenStack Platform Administrator, I want to import existing OpenStack resources into ORC management without recreating them, so that I can adopt ORC in an environment with pre-existing infrastructure. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given an existing OpenStack network and an ORC Network CR with {{spec.import.filter.name}} matching that network, then ORC adopts the network without recreating it and sets {{.status.id}} to the existing UUID.   - Given a filter that matches more than one OpenStack resource, then ORC sets a terminal error condition and does not adopt any resource.   - Given a successfully imported resource, then subsequent reconciliation enforces the desired spec against the imported resource.

*US-004*: As a Platform Engineering / DevOps Engineer, I want to manage OpenStack credentials via Kubernetes Secrets referenced by ORC CRs so that I can use existing secret management tooling (Vault, SealedSecrets) without embedding credentials in CR manifests. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given a Kubernetes Secret containing a valid {{clouds.yaml}}, when referenced via {{spec.cloudCredentialsRef}}, then ORC authenticates all OpenStack API calls for that CR using those credentials.   - Given an invalid or expired credential Secret, then ORC sets a terminal {{Available=False}} condition with a clear authentication error message — without logging credential values.

*US-005*: As an OpenStack Platform Administrator, I want a published maturity matrix so that I can determine which ORC controllers are safe to use for evaluation and which to avoid. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given the Tech Preview documentation, every shipped controller is listed with its maturity status and known limitations.   - Given I look up the Server controller, I can immediately see whether it is included and what constraints apply.

----

h2. 7. Scope

h3. In Scope

* Packaging and shipping the ORC operator (based on {{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}} v2.x) for installation on a supported Kubernetes/OpenShift cluster via a server-side-apply release manifest.
* Tech Preview support for the following controllers (subject to final maturity review against the pinned upstream commit at engineering kick-off):
** *Network* (Neutron) — partially implemented upstream; core create/update/delete validated
** *Subnet* (Neutron) — partially implemented; update support present
** *Router* (Neutron) — partially implemented; interface attachment via RouterInterface
** *RouterInterface* (Neutron) — sub-resource for router/subnet attachment
** *SecurityGroup* (Neutron, including rules) — mostly implemented upstream
** *Image* (Glance) — mostly implemented; URL-based upload, hash verification
** *Flavor* (Nova) — mostly implemented; immutable field handling
** *AddressScope* (Neutron) — mostly implemented
** *Trunk* (Neutron) — mostly implemented; sub-port management
* Documentation: installation guide, controller reference (per-controller CRD field reference), maturity matrix, known limitations, and troubleshooting guide.
* Clear Tech Preview designation with associated support boundary communicated to customers in all docs and the product portal.
* QE validation of included controllers on a supported RHOSP and OpenShift version combination.
* Multi-platform container image support (amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x).

h3. Out of Scope

* General Availability (GA) of ORC — this PRD covers Tech Preview only.
* Production-level support SLAs.
* Controllers assessed as not mature enough for Tech Preview (to be documented explicitly in the maturity matrix):
** *Port* (Neutron) — partially implemented; complex field surface area; deferred to Non-MVP
** *FloatingIP* (Neutron) — partially implemented; association/disassociation completeness under review
** *KeyPair* (Nova) — partially implemented; deferred to Non-MVP
** *Server* (Nova) — partially implemented; complex multi-resource dependency graph; deferred to Non-MVP
** *ServerGroup* (Nova) — mostly implemented but requires Server controller maturity for full validation
** *Volume* / *VolumeType* (Cinder) — partially implemented; deferred to Non-MVP
** *Project* (Keystone) — partially implemented; domain scoping in progress
** *Domain*, *Group*, *Role*, *Service* (Keystone) — identity management controllers; deferred
** *ApplicationCredential*, *Endpoint*, *User* (Keystone) — partially implemented; deferred
* Drift detection (active upstream enhancement proposal; not yet implemented; planned for post-Tech Preview)
* Migration tooling to convert existing Heat/Ansible-managed resources to ORC CRs
* Multi-cloud or non-OpenStack resource management
* Integration with specific GitOps platforms (ArgoCD, Flux) beyond documentation guidance
* ORC as a drop-in replacement for CAPO in this release

----

h2. 8. Assumptions & Constraints

h3. Assumptions

* The upstream {{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}} project remains Apache 2.0 licensed and Red Hat engineers (including active maintainer Martin André) continue upstream contribution, enabling productization without forking.
* The upstream {{v1alpha1}} API will not undergo breaking structural changes between the Tech Preview branch point and ship date; the project's semver policy prohibits breaking changes within a major version.
* Customers evaluating Tech Preview have an existing, operational RHOSP deployment and a Kubernetes/OpenShift cluster (v1.29+) to serve as the management control plane.
* Tech Preview customers understand that Tech Preview features are not covered by production support SLAs.
* Controllers selected for Tech Preview inclusion will have zero known P1 correctness bugs and will pass QE's create/update/delete/no-op/import test scenarios.

h3. Constraints

* *Tech Preview support boundary*: ORC is explicitly not supported for production workloads under standard Red Hat subscriptions.
* *API stability*: All ORC CRDs are at {{openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1}}. No upstream stability guarantee exists. Upgrades between Tech Preview versions may require CR migration; this must be communicated in the release notes.
* *Kubernetes version floor*: ORC requires Kubernetes v1.29+ due to CEL validation. This sets the minimum OpenShift version for the Tech Preview.
* *Namespace scoping*: ORC enforces same-namespace references for all CRs and credential Secrets. Cross-namespace management scenarios are not supported.
* *No OpenStack UUIDs in spec*: ORC enforces (via API linter) that OpenStack resource IDs never appear in {{.spec}} fields. All cross-resource references use ORC object names. This is a deliberate API design constraint, not a limitation.

h3. Dependencies

* Upstream {{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}} project (v2.x, pinned commit) for source code, CRD definitions, and container images.
* Red Hat OpenStack Platform (RHOSP) — specific tested version(s) to be confirmed during QE planning (minimum: OpenStack Nova Stein-era APIs or later).
* OpenShift/Kubernetes — minimum v1.29; target cluster version to be confirmed at engineering kick-off.
* Gophercloud v2 ({{github.com/gophercloud/gophercloud/v2}}) — ORC's OpenStack Go SDK; upstream project dependency.
* Red Hat documentation team for customer-facing documentation authoring and review.
* QE team for validation test planning and execution.

----

h2. 9. Risks & Mitigations

||Risk||Likelihood||Impact||Mitigation||
|Upstream releases v3 with minor breaking API changes before the Tech Preview ships, invalidating QE results|Medium|High|Pin the Tech Preview to a specific upstream release tag (v2.5.x); track the v3 roadmap; maintain a productization branch so upstream breaking changes do not automatically flow in.|
|A controller included in Tech Preview has a latent data-loss bug (e.g., deletes an OpenStack resource it should not on CR deletion)|Low|High|Every included controller must pass a full create/update/delete/no-op/import test matrix in a real OpenStack environment before ship; gate on zero P1 bugs.|
|Customer confusion about Tech Preview vs. GA support leads to unsupported production deployments|Medium|Medium|Mandatory Tech Preview disclaimer in product documentation, portal, and release notes; clear guidance on upgrade path to GA when available.|
|Upstream project maturity for Non-MVP controllers (Port, Server, KeyPair) advances rapidly and customer demand drives premature GA promotion|Low|Medium|Maintain a living maturity matrix updated per release; define an explicit GA promotion criteria checklist (API graduation to v1beta1, N-release soak time, test coverage threshold).|

----

h2. 10. Controller Maturity Matrix

The following table reflects the upstream ORC project state at *v2.5.0 (April 16, 2026)* — the most recent release at PRD authoring. The upstream README uses a two-level maturity marker: ✔ (mostly implemented) and ◐ (partially implemented). A formal engineering review against the pinned upstream commit must be conducted at Tech Preview engineering kick-off, and this table must be updated at that point.

||Controller||OpenStack Service||API Version||Upstream Maturity||Tech Preview Status||Notes||
|Network|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Create/update/delete and import present; project-scoping supported; full field coverage under review.|
|Subnet|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Update support added in v2.3; network dependency ordering enforced.|
|Router|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Core lifecycle complete; subnet interface management via RouterInterface CR.|
|RouterInterface|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Sub-resource of Router; manages router-subnet attachment lifecycle.|
|SecurityGroup (incl. rules)|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Inline rule management fully reconciled; create/update/delete complete.|
|Image|Glance|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|URL-based image upload, hash verification, large image handling validated. Shipped since ORC v1.0.0.|
|Flavor|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Create/delete complete; immutable fields reported as terminal errors; extra specs supported.|
|AddressScope|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Added in v2.5.0; create/delete lifecycle complete.|
|Trunk|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Added in v2.5.0; parent port reference and sub-port management complete.|
|Port|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Large field surface (14KB type definition); {{valueSpecs}}, port binding, MAC address added in v2.5; requires additional validation.|
|FloatingIP|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.2.0; allocation and port association present; additional lifecycle edge cases under review.|
|KeyPair|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; basic create/delete complete; Secret-based key import validation in progress.|
|Server|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Complex multi-resource dependency graph; volume attach/detach, interface attach/detach, configdrive, and metadata added in v2.3–v2.5; insufficient soak time for Tech Preview inclusion.|
|ServerGroup|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Functionally complete but practical validation requires Server controller maturity.|
|Volume|Cinder|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.3.0; bootable-from-image creation supported; availability zone configurable; additional field coverage in progress.|
|VolumeType|Cinder|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.3.0; basic lifecycle present; limited real-world validation.|
|Project|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.1.0; {{domainRef}} added in v2.5; identity management scope requires additional review.|
|Domain|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; identity management controllers deferred from initial Tech Preview.|
|Group|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; deferred with other identity controllers.|
|Role|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; deferred with other identity controllers.|
|Service|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; deferred with other identity controllers.|
|ApplicationCredential|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; sensitive credential management requires security review.|
|Endpoint|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; deferred with identity controllers.|
|User|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; sensitive identity management; requires security review.|

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Note*: "Candidate — Included" status is conditional on a formal engineering maturity review against the pinned upstream commit at Tech Preview engineering kick-off. This table must be updated at that milestone to reflect the actual ship-time assessment. All API versions are {{openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1}}; no upstream graduation timeline to v1beta1 is currently defined.
{panel}

----

h2. 11. Glossary

||Term||Definition||
|ORC|OpenStack Resource Controller — the upstream Kubernetes operator at {{github.com/k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}}.|
|CRD|Custom Resource Definition — a Kubernetes extension mechanism for defining new resource types.|
|CR|Custom Resource — an instance of a CRD applied to the Kubernetes API to declare desired state.|
|Tech Preview|A Red Hat designation for features available for customer evaluation but not covered by production support SLAs.|
|Reconciliation|The process by which ORC compares the declared desired state (CR spec) against the actual state (OpenStack API) and converges them.|
|CAPO|Cluster API Provider OpenStack — a Kubernetes Cluster API implementation for OpenStack; a production consumer of ORC.|
|clouds.yaml|The standard OpenStack client configuration file format containing credentials and endpoint information for one or more OpenStack clouds.|
|GitOps|An operational model where infrastructure desired state is declared in Git and automated systems continuously reconcile actual state to match.|
|Gophercloud|The Go SDK for OpenStack, used by ORC to communicate with OpenStack APIs.|
|SSA|Server-Side Apply — the Kubernetes API mechanism used to install ORC ({{kubectl apply --server-side}}).|
|Management Policy|A per-CR ORC field ({{managementPolicy}}) that controls whether ORC actively manages ({{managed}}) or only tracks ({{unmanaged}}) the corresponding OpenStack resource.|
|Terminal Error|An ORC error classification indicating that retrying will not resolve the condition (e.g., invalid spec, permanently missing referenced resource). Requires user intervention.|

----

_This document is a living draft. It must be reviewed and approved by Engineering, Product Management, Documentation, and QE leads before the Tech Preview engineering phase begins. The Controller Maturity Matrix in Section 10 must be re-validated against the pinned upstream commit at engineering kick-off._
items.toString:
h2. 2. Problem Statement

h3. 2.1 Current State

Administrators managing Red Hat OpenStack Platform today rely on Heat templates, Ansible playbooks, or direct OpenStack API/CLI calls to provision and lifecycle-manage infrastructure resources. These approaches are imperative, difficult to reconcile against desired state, and do not integrate natively with Kubernetes-based GitOps workflows that many organizations are adopting.

The upstream ORC project ({{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}}) exists and is actively developed — it has reached v2.5.0 as of April 2026, with 24 implemented controllers spanning Neutron, Nova, Glance, Cinder, and Keystone. It is already consumed in production by Cluster API Provider OpenStack (CAPO). However, it is not productized by Red Hat, has no customer-facing support boundary, and is not shipped as part of any RHOSP release.

h3. 2.2 Desired State

Red Hat ships a Tech Preview of ORC as part of its OpenStack product offering. Customers who use Kubernetes as a control plane can declare OpenStack infrastructure resources as Kubernetes objects, have them continuously reconciled, and integrate OpenStack provisioning into existing GitOps pipelines (ArgoCD, Flux). The Tech Preview clearly communicates which controllers are ready for evaluation and which remain experimental.

h3. 2.3 Business Impact

* Enables RHOSP customers to adopt cloud-native, declarative infrastructure management without abandoning their OpenStack investment.
* Aligns with the CAPO strategic direction, where ORC is already the resource management dependency layer in production.
* Reduces configuration drift incidents by enabling continuous desired-state reconciliation.
* Provides a differentiated capability not currently offered by competitors at a productized level.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Note*: This ticket has been identified as a duplicate of RHOSTRAT-632 and is being closed accordingly. The canonical PRD is tracked under RHOSTRAT-632. All future review, revision, and approval activity should occur on that ticket.
{panel}

----

h2. 3. Goals & Objectives

h3. Primary Goals

* Package and ship ORC as a Tech Preview feature accessible to RHOSP customers.
* Define the subset of the 24 upstream controllers mature enough for Tech Preview inclusion and explicitly exclude those that are not.
* Communicate the maturity status of each included controller clearly in documentation.
* Establish a Tech Preview support boundary (community-level, best-effort) and ensure customers understand it.
* Provide installation, configuration, and usage documentation sufficient for non-production evaluation.

h3. Success Metrics

||Metric||Current||Target||Measurement Method||
|Controllers included in Tech Preview|0 (not productized)|≥ 8 controllers based on upstream maturity assessment|Controller maturity review at ship time|
|Customer adoption|0|≥ 5 customer environments within 90 days of Tech Preview ship|Telemetry / customer success reports|
|P1 bugs in included controllers at ship|Unknown|0|Bug tracker at release|
|Documentation completeness|0%|100% of included controllers documented with examples|Doc review gate|
|Time to first reconciled resource (new install)|N/A|≤ 30 minutes following documented install steps|QE validation|

----

h2. 4. User Personas

h3. Persona 1: OpenStack Platform Administrator

* *Role*: Infrastructure engineer or cloud administrator managing a RHOSP environment.
* *Goals*: Provision and lifecycle-manage OpenStack resources (networks, subnets, routers, security groups, images, flavors) in a repeatable, auditable, declarative manner — without writing Heat templates or imperative scripts.
* *Pain Points*: Current tooling (Heat, Ansible, CLI) does not integrate with GitOps workflows; configuration drift is hard to detect and remediate; there is no continuous reconciliation of declared vs. actual state.
* *Usage Context*: Uses a Kubernetes cluster as a control plane alongside an existing RHOSP deployment; wants to store OpenStack resource definitions in Git and have them automatically applied and reconciled.

h3. Persona 2: Platform Engineering / DevOps Engineer

* *Role*: Engineer responsible for integrating infrastructure provisioning into CI/CD and GitOps pipelines.
* *Goals*: Treat OpenStack infrastructure as code using Kubernetes-native manifests; integrate OpenStack provisioning into ArgoCD or Flux pipelines alongside application deployments.
* *Pain Points*: No Kubernetes-native way to manage OpenStack resources; forced to maintain separate tooling stacks (Terraform, Ansible) outside the GitOps control plane.
* *Usage Context*: Defines OpenStack CRs in a Git repository; a GitOps operator syncs them to a management Kubernetes cluster running ORC; ORC reconciles desired state against the OpenStack API.

----

h2. 5. Requirements

h3. 5.1 Functional Requirements

||ID||Requirement||Priority||Acceptance Criteria||
|FR-001|ORC must be installable on a supported Kubernetes/OpenShift cluster via a defined, documented method (server-side apply of a release manifest bundle).|MVP|Installation procedure documented; QE can complete installation in a clean environment following only the documentation.|
|FR-002|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Network* resources (create, update, delete, reconcile).|MVP|A Network CR can be applied; ORC creates the corresponding OpenStack network; deletion of the CR removes the network; existing networks can be imported by filter or by name.|
|FR-003|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Subnet* resources (create, update, delete, reconcile).|MVP|A Subnet CR can be applied referencing a Network CR; ORC creates the subnet in the correct network; cross-resource dependency ordering is enforced.|
|FR-004|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Router* resources and their subnet interface attachments via *RouterInterface* resources.|MVP|A Router CR can be applied; ORC creates the router; RouterInterface CRs attach subnets to the router in the correct order.|
|FR-005|ORC must support management of OpenStack *SecurityGroup* resources, including inline security group rules.|MVP|A SecurityGroup CR can be applied; ORC creates the security group and all specified rules; updates to rules are reconciled correctly.|
|FR-006|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Image* (Glance) resources including upload from a remote URL source.|MVP|An Image CR can be applied referencing an image source URL; ORC downloads and registers the image in Glance; image hash verification is performed if specified.|
|FR-007|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Flavor* resources (create, delete; immutable fields enforced).|MVP|A Flavor CR can be applied; ORC creates the Nova flavor; attempts to update immutable fields are reported as a terminal error, not silently ignored.|
|FR-008|ORC must support management of OpenStack *AddressScope* (Neutron) resources.|MVP|An AddressScope CR can be applied; ORC creates the address scope; deletion removes it from Neutron.|
|FR-009|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Trunk* (Neutron) resources.|MVP|A Trunk CR can be applied referencing a parent Port CR; ORC creates the trunk and sub-ports.|
|FR-010|ORC must expose standard Kubernetes status conditions on each CR ({{Progressing}}, {{Available}}) reflecting actual reconciliation state.|MVP|All CRs surface {{.status.conditions}}; {{Available=True}} is set when the resource is ready; error conditions include a human-readable message referencing the OpenStack API response.|
|FR-011|ORC must store the OpenStack UUID of each managed resource in {{.status.id}} after successful creation.|MVP|After a resource is created, {{.status.id}} contains the UUID; {{.status.resource}} reflects the full observed OpenStack state.|
|FR-012|ORC must support referencing OpenStack credentials via a Kubernetes Secret (containing a {{clouds.yaml}}) on each CR via a {{cloudCredentialsRef}} field.|MVP|A valid Secret is referenced; ORC authenticates using those credentials; an invalid or expired credential is reflected as a terminal error condition on the CR.|
|FR-013|ORC must support importing existing OpenStack resources into management without recreating them, using either a name/filter-based import or direct ID import.|MVP|A CR with {{spec.import}} referencing an existing OpenStack resource causes ORC to adopt that resource; no recreation occurs; filter matching more than one resource produces a terminal error.|
|FR-014|ORC must support a management policy field per CR that allows unmanaged mode (status-tracking only, no modification).|MVP|A CR with {{managementPolicy: unmanaged}} causes ORC to track and report resource status without modifying the OpenStack resource.|
|FR-015|ORC must handle transient OpenStack API errors with retry and exponential backoff; permanent errors must surface as terminal conditions without infinite crash-looping.|MVP|Transient errors (network timeouts) cause retry; 409 Neutron quota-exceeded errors are treated as retryable; non-retryable errors produce a terminal {{Available=False}} condition.|
|FR-016|The Tech Preview release must include documentation clearly identifying each included controller's maturity status (Tech Preview / Experimental / Not Included).|MVP|A maturity matrix is published with the Tech Preview; every controller is labeled; known limitations per controller are documented.|
|FR-017|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Port* (Neutron) resources.|Non-MVP|A Port CR can be applied referencing a Network and optionally a Subnet; ORC creates the Neutron port; IP addresses, port security, VNIC type, and {{valueSpecs}} are configurable.|
|FR-018|ORC must support management of OpenStack *FloatingIP* (Neutron) resources.|Non-MVP|A FloatingIP CR can be applied; ORC allocates a floating IP from a specified network and optionally associates it with a Port CR.|
|FR-019|ORC must support management of OpenStack *KeyPair* (Nova) resources.|Non-MVP|A KeyPair CR can be applied; ORC creates the keypair in Nova; the public key may be provided inline or referenced from a Secret.|
|FR-020|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Server* (Nova) resources.|Non-MVP|A Server CR can be applied specifying flavor, image, network interfaces, keypair, and availability zone; ORC creates the Nova instance; Server waits for dependent ORC resources to be Available before provisioning.|
|FR-021|ORC must support management of OpenStack *ServerGroup* (Nova) resources.|Non-MVP|A ServerGroup CR can be applied with a specified policy (e.g., anti-affinity, affinity, soft variants); ORC creates the server group; Server CRs can reference a ServerGroup CR.|
|FR-022|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Volume* (Cinder) resources, including creation of bootable volumes from images.|Non-MVP|A Volume CR can be applied specifying size, type, and optionally an image source; ORC creates the Cinder volume; availability zone is configurable.|
|FR-023|ORC must support management of OpenStack *Project* (Keystone) resources.|Non-MVP|A Project CR can be applied; ORC creates the Keystone project; {{domainRef}} is supported for domain-scoped projects.|

h3. 5.2 Non-Functional Requirements

||ID||Requirement||Category||Target||
|NFR-001|ORC must not modify or delete OpenStack resources it does not manage. Resources with no corresponding ORC CR must never be affected by ORC operations.|Safety|Zero unintended deletions of unmanaged resources during QE validation.|
|NFR-002|ORC must document that Tech Preview is not covered by Red Hat production support SLAs; this disclaimer must appear in all installation documentation and on the product page.|Supportability|Tech Preview disclaimer visible in all installation docs; QE review gate.|
|NFR-003|ORC reconciliation must complete a no-op pass (resource already in desired state) for non-image resources within 30 seconds under normal conditions.|Performance|Measured during QE validation on a representative environment.|
|NFR-004|ORC must enforce namespace-scoped operation: all cross-resource references (other ORC CRs, credential Secrets) must reside in the same namespace as the referencing CR.|Security|Cross-namespace references are rejected by admission validation; no cluster-admin privileges required for namespace-scoped operation.|
|NFR-005|ORC must log reconciliation events and errors in a structured format compatible with standard Kubernetes log aggregation; log level must be configurable; errors must include the resource name/namespace and the OpenStack request ID.|Observability|Logs are structured JSON or key=value; OpenStack {{Request-ID}} is surfaced in error logs (enabled via ReconcileID forwarding).|
|NFR-006|ORC must run on Kubernetes v1.29 or later (required for CEL validation support).|Compatibility|QE validates against the minimum supported OpenShift version at Tech Preview ship time; CEL validation is tested.|
|NFR-007|ORC must not expose OpenStack API credentials in Kubernetes event logs or status conditions.|Security|Credential values never appear in {{.status}}, events, or controller logs; only error summaries (not raw API responses containing credentials) are surfaced.|

----

h2. 6. User Stories

*US-001*: As an OpenStack Platform Administrator, I want to define Network, Subnet, and Router resources as Kubernetes manifests so that I can manage OpenStack network topology declaratively and store it in Git. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given a valid Network CR applied to the cluster, when ORC reconciles it, then the corresponding OpenStack network exists with the specified properties.   - Given a Subnet CR referencing that Network CR, when the Network CR is Available, then ORC creates the subnet in the correct network — without requiring manual ordering.   - Given the Network CR is deleted while a Subnet CR still references it, when ORC processes the deletion, then the Network deletion is blocked until the Subnet CR is removed first.   - Given the OpenStack network already exists with the desired properties, when ORC reconciles, then no changes are made and the CR status shows {{Available=True}}.

*US-002*: As a Platform Engineering / DevOps Engineer, I want ORC CRs to expose standard Kubernetes status conditions so that I can integrate OpenStack resource readiness into GitOps health checks and pipeline gates. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given a CR is successfully reconciled, then {{Available=True}} is set on the CR with a timestamp.   - Given a CR fails to reconcile due to an OpenStack API error, then the {{Available=False}} condition includes an actionable message and the OpenStack request ID for correlation.   - Given an ArgoCD Application monitors ORC CRs, when all CRs are {{Available=True}}, then ArgoCD reports the Application as Healthy.

*US-003*: As an OpenStack Platform Administrator, I want to import existing OpenStack resources into ORC management without recreating them, so that I can adopt ORC in an environment with pre-existing infrastructure. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given an existing OpenStack network and an ORC Network CR with {{spec.import.filter.name}} matching that network, then ORC adopts the network without recreating it and sets {{.status.id}} to the existing UUID.   - Given a filter that matches more than one OpenStack resource, then ORC sets a terminal error condition and does not adopt any resource.   - Given a successfully imported resource, then subsequent reconciliation enforces the desired spec against the imported resource.

*US-004*: As a Platform Engineering / DevOps Engineer, I want to manage OpenStack credentials via Kubernetes Secrets referenced by ORC CRs so that I can use existing secret management tooling (Vault, SealedSecrets) without embedding credentials in CR manifests. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given a Kubernetes Secret containing a valid {{clouds.yaml}}, when referenced via {{spec.cloudCredentialsRef}}, then ORC authenticates all OpenStack API calls for that CR using those credentials.   - Given an invalid or expired credential Secret, then ORC sets a terminal {{Available=False}} condition with a clear authentication error message — without logging credential values.

*US-005*: As an OpenStack Platform Administrator, I want a published maturity matrix so that I can determine which ORC controllers are safe to use for evaluation and which to avoid. - *Acceptance Criteria*:   - Given the Tech Preview documentation, every shipped controller is listed with its maturity status and known limitations.   - Given I look up the Server controller, I can immediately see whether it is included and what constraints apply.

----

h2. 7. Scope

h3. In Scope

* Packaging and shipping the ORC operator (based on {{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}} v2.x) for installation on a supported Kubernetes/OpenShift cluster via a server-side-apply release manifest.
* Tech Preview support for the following controllers (subject to final maturity review against the pinned upstream commit at engineering kick-off):
** *Network* (Neutron) — partially implemented upstream; core create/update/delete validated
** *Subnet* (Neutron) — partially implemented; update support present
** *Router* (Neutron) — partially implemented; interface attachment via RouterInterface
** *RouterInterface* (Neutron) — sub-resource for router/subnet attachment
** *SecurityGroup* (Neutron, including rules) — mostly implemented upstream
** *Image* (Glance) — mostly implemented; URL-based upload, hash verification
** *Flavor* (Nova) — mostly implemented; immutable field handling
** *AddressScope* (Neutron) — mostly implemented
** *Trunk* (Neutron) — mostly implemented; sub-port management
* Documentation: installation guide, controller reference (per-controller CRD field reference), maturity matrix, known limitations, and troubleshooting guide.
* Clear Tech Preview designation with associated support boundary communicated to customers in all docs and the product portal.
* QE validation of included controllers on a supported RHOSP and OpenShift version combination.
* Multi-platform container image support (amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x).

h3. Out of Scope

* General Availability (GA) of ORC — this PRD covers Tech Preview only.
* Production-level support SLAs.
* Controllers assessed as not mature enough for Tech Preview (to be documented explicitly in the maturity matrix):
** *Port* (Neutron) — partially implemented; complex field surface area; deferred to Non-MVP
** *FloatingIP* (Neutron) — partially implemented; association/disassociation completeness under review
** *KeyPair* (Nova) — partially implemented; deferred to Non-MVP
** *Server* (Nova) — partially implemented; complex multi-resource dependency graph; deferred to Non-MVP
** *ServerGroup* (Nova) — mostly implemented but requires Server controller maturity for full validation
** *Volume* / *VolumeType* (Cinder) — partially implemented; deferred to Non-MVP
** *Project* (Keystone) — partially implemented; domain scoping in progress
** *Domain*, *Group*, *Role*, *Service* (Keystone) — identity management controllers; deferred
** *ApplicationCredential*, *Endpoint*, *User* (Keystone) — partially implemented; deferred
* Drift detection (active upstream enhancement proposal; not yet implemented; planned for post-Tech Preview)
* Migration tooling to convert existing Heat/Ansible-managed resources to ORC CRs
* Multi-cloud or non-OpenStack resource management
* Integration with specific GitOps platforms (ArgoCD, Flux) beyond documentation guidance
* ORC as a drop-in replacement for CAPO in this release

----

h2. 8. Assumptions & Constraints

h3. Assumptions

* The upstream {{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}} project remains Apache 2.0 licensed and Red Hat engineers (including active maintainer Martin André) continue upstream contribution, enabling productization without forking.
* The upstream {{v1alpha1}} API will not undergo breaking structural changes between the Tech Preview branch point and ship date; the project's semver policy prohibits breaking changes within a major version.
* Customers evaluating Tech Preview have an existing, operational RHOSP deployment and a Kubernetes/OpenShift cluster (v1.29+) to serve as the management control plane.
* Tech Preview customers understand that Tech Preview features are not covered by production support SLAs.
* Controllers selected for Tech Preview inclusion will have zero known P1 correctness bugs and will pass QE's create/update/delete/no-op/import test scenarios.

h3. Constraints

* *Tech Preview support boundary*: ORC is explicitly not supported for production workloads under standard Red Hat subscriptions.
* *API stability*: All ORC CRDs are at {{openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1}}. No upstream stability guarantee exists. Upgrades between Tech Preview versions may require CR migration; this must be communicated in the release notes.
* *Kubernetes version floor*: ORC requires Kubernetes v1.29+ due to CEL validation. This sets the minimum OpenShift version for the Tech Preview.
* *Namespace scoping*: ORC enforces same-namespace references for all CRs and credential Secrets. Cross-namespace management scenarios are not supported.
* *No OpenStack UUIDs in spec*: ORC enforces (via API linter) that OpenStack resource IDs never appear in {{.spec}} fields. All cross-resource references use ORC object names. This is a deliberate API design constraint, not a limitation.

h3. Dependencies

* Upstream {{k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}} project (v2.x, pinned commit) for source code, CRD definitions, and container images.
* Red Hat OpenStack Platform (RHOSP) — specific tested version(s) to be confirmed during QE planning (minimum: OpenStack Nova Stein-era APIs or later).
* OpenShift/Kubernetes — minimum v1.29; target cluster version to be confirmed at engineering kick-off.
* Gophercloud v2 ({{github.com/gophercloud/gophercloud/v2}}) — ORC's OpenStack Go SDK; upstream project dependency.
* Red Hat documentation team for customer-facing documentation authoring and review.
* QE team for validation test planning and execution.

----

h2. 9. Risks & Mitigations

||Risk||Likelihood||Impact||Mitigation||
|Upstream releases v3 with minor breaking API changes before the Tech Preview ships, invalidating QE results|Medium|High|Pin the Tech Preview to a specific upstream release tag (v2.5.x); track the v3 roadmap; maintain a productization branch so upstream breaking changes do not automatically flow in.|
|A controller included in Tech Preview has a latent data-loss bug (e.g., deletes an OpenStack resource it should not on CR deletion)|Low|High|Every included controller must pass a full create/update/delete/no-op/import test matrix in a real OpenStack environment before ship; gate on zero P1 bugs.|
|Customer confusion about Tech Preview vs. GA support leads to unsupported production deployments|Medium|Medium|Mandatory Tech Preview disclaimer in product documentation, portal, and release notes; clear guidance on upgrade path to GA when available.|
|Upstream project maturity for Non-MVP controllers (Port, Server, KeyPair) advances rapidly and customer demand drives premature GA promotion|Low|Medium|Maintain a living maturity matrix updated per release; define an explicit GA promotion criteria checklist (API graduation to v1beta1, N-release soak time, test coverage threshold).|

----

h2. 10. Controller Maturity Matrix

The following table reflects the upstream ORC project state at *v2.5.0 (April 16, 2026)* — the most recent release at PRD authoring. The upstream README uses a two-level maturity marker: ✔ (mostly implemented) and ◐ (partially implemented). A formal engineering review against the pinned upstream commit must be conducted at Tech Preview engineering kick-off, and this table must be updated at that point.

||Controller||OpenStack Service||API Version||Upstream Maturity||Tech Preview Status||Notes||
|Network|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Create/update/delete and import present; project-scoping supported; full field coverage under review.|
|Subnet|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Update support added in v2.3; network dependency ordering enforced.|
|Router|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Core lifecycle complete; subnet interface management via RouterInterface CR.|
|RouterInterface|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Candidate — Included*|Sub-resource of Router; manages router-subnet attachment lifecycle.|
|SecurityGroup (incl. rules)|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Inline rule management fully reconciled; create/update/delete complete.|
|Image|Glance|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|URL-based image upload, hash verification, large image handling validated. Shipped since ORC v1.0.0.|
|Flavor|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Create/delete complete; immutable fields reported as terminal errors; extra specs supported.|
|AddressScope|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Added in v2.5.0; create/delete lifecycle complete.|
|Trunk|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Candidate — Included*|Added in v2.5.0; parent port reference and sub-port management complete.|
|Port|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Large field surface (14KB type definition); {{valueSpecs}}, port binding, MAC address added in v2.5; requires additional validation.|
|FloatingIP|Neutron|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.2.0; allocation and port association present; additional lifecycle edge cases under review.|
|KeyPair|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; basic create/delete complete; Secret-based key import validation in progress.|
|Server|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Complex multi-resource dependency graph; volume attach/detach, interface attach/detach, configdrive, and metadata added in v2.3–v2.5; insufficient soak time for Tech Preview inclusion.|
|ServerGroup|Nova|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Functionally complete but practical validation requires Server controller maturity.|
|Volume|Cinder|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.3.0; bootable-from-image creation supported; availability zone configurable; additional field coverage in progress.|
|VolumeType|Cinder|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.3.0; basic lifecycle present; limited real-world validation.|
|Project|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.1.0; {{domainRef}} added in v2.5; identity management scope requires additional review.|
|Domain|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; identity management controllers deferred from initial Tech Preview.|
|Group|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; deferred with other identity controllers.|
|Role|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.4.0; deferred with other identity controllers.|
|Service|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|✔ Mostly complete|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; deferred with other identity controllers.|
|ApplicationCredential|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; sensitive credential management requires security review.|
|Endpoint|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; deferred with identity controllers.|
|User|Keystone|openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1|◐ Partial|*Not Included — Deferred*|Added in v2.5.0; sensitive identity management; requires security review.|

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Note*: "Candidate — Included" status is conditional on a formal engineering maturity review against the pinned upstream commit at Tech Preview engineering kick-off. This table must be updated at that milestone to reflect the actual ship-time assessment. All API versions are {{openstack.k-orc.cloud/v1alpha1}}; no upstream graduation timeline to v1beta1 is currently defined.
{panel}

----

h2. 11. Glossary

||Term||Definition||
|ORC|OpenStack Resource Controller — the upstream Kubernetes operator at {{github.com/k-orc/openstack-resource-controller}}.|
|CRD|Custom Resource Definition — a Kubernetes extension mechanism for defining new resource types.|
|CR|Custom Resource — an instance of a CRD applied to the Kubernetes API to declare desired state.|
|Tech Preview|A Red Hat designation for features available for customer evaluation but not covered by production support SLAs.|
|Reconciliation|The process by which ORC compares the declared desired state (CR spec) against the actual state (OpenStack API) and converges them.|
|CAPO|Cluster API Provider OpenStack — a Kubernetes Cluster API implementation for OpenStack; a production consumer of ORC.|
|clouds.yaml|The standard OpenStack client configuration file format containing credentials and endpoint information for one or more OpenStack clouds.|
|GitOps|An operational model where infrastructure desired state is declared in Git and automated systems continuously reconcile actual state to match.|
|Gophercloud|The Go SDK for OpenStack, used by ORC to communicate with OpenStack APIs.|
|SSA|Server-Side Apply — the Kubernetes API mechanism used to install ORC ({{kubectl apply --server-side}}).|
|Management Policy|A per-CR ORC field ({{managementPolicy}}) that controls whether ORC actively manages ({{managed}}) or only tracks ({{unmanaged}}) the corresponding OpenStack resource.|
|Terminal Error|An ORC error classification indicating that retrying will not resolve the condition (e.g., invalid spec, permanently missing referenced resource). Requires user intervention.|

----

_This document is a living draft. It must be reviewed and approved by Engineering, Product Management, Documentation, and QE leads before the Tech Preview engineering phase begins. The Controller Maturity Matrix in Section 10 must be re-validated against the pinned upstream commit at engineering kick-off._
