 ## Check that NVIDIA drivers load properly inside the guest OS.
 # vGPU Assignment
 ## Create vGPUs on RTX PRO 6000
 ## Confirm successful vGPUs allocation to VMs.
 ## Ensure virtual machines boot correctly with assigned GPU(s).
 ## Check that NVIDIA drivers load properly inside the guest OS.

*Deliverable 2 - Documentation Package* 
 # Host Setup Guide
 ## Ex BIOS settings, Kernel parameter requirements
 ## How to install vGPU driver and divide GPU to vGPUs
 # GPU Partition Configuration Guide
 ## How to create divide GPU to vGPUs
 ## Examples for flavor, aggregate, and placement mapping, Example VM launches
 # Troubleshooting Guide
 ## Document any issues discovered during verification process

 
{*}O{*}{*}ut of Scope:{*}
 * This initiative is strictly for purpose of verification of capabilities of currently available components within RHOSO-18.0 and no implementation work is expected

 * This is requested as one time validation before datacenter deployment and does not require recurrent CI job

items.fromString:
h3. *Feature Request Overview*

RHOSO customers are evaluating Red Hat OpenStack (RHOSO) as the virtualization platform for NVIDIA GPU-based AI services. They require support for both HGX B300 platforms and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, with specific expectations around VM-level GPU assignment and multi-tenancy. This RFE requests clarification, tracking, and enablement work required in OpenStack to support these use cases.
h3. *Customer/Business Context*
 * Customer: (AI infrastructure services)

 * Platform under evaluation: Red Hat OpenStack (RHOSO)

 * Drivers: AI workload virtualization, GPU multi-tenancy, predictable performance

 * Non-goals: BMaaS, ARM CPUs, multi-node GPU pooling

The customer is comparing OpenStack and OpenShift Virtualization and needs a clear statement of what is achievable in OpenStack, what requires engineering work, and realistic timelines.
h3. *Hardware in Scope*

*1. NVIDIA HGX B300 (Blackwell, NVLink-based)*
 * 8-GPU NVLink/NVSwitch-based platform

 * Fabric Manager required

 * Single-node focus (no multi-node GPU pooling)

*2. NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe)*
 * Discrete PCIe GPU

 * Standard enterprise virtualization use cases

h3. *Functional requirements* 

*1. HGX B300 Requirements*

*Must Have*
 * Ability to assign GPUs to VMs

 * Support *GPU passthrough* on HGX B300 systems

 * NVIDIA Fabric Manager integration on compute hosts

*Critical Requirement*
 * *NVLink multi-tenancy*
NVLink connectivity must be {*}partitioned between VMs{*}, so that:
 ** GPUs assigned to different VMs are not fully NVLink-coherent
 ** One VM does not gain implicit access to GPUs assigned to another VM

*Explicitly NOT Required*
 * Topology-aware scheduling

 * Multi-node GPU fabrics

 * Cross-host NVLink

 * Disaggregated GPU pooling

 

*2. RTX PRO 6000 Requirements*

*Must Have*
 * GPU assignment to VMs via PCI passthrough

*Nice to Have / Future*
 * vGPU support (time-sliced or mediated device)

 * Live migration is not a hard requirement for initial deployment

h3. *Key Questions for Engineering*

This RFE explicitly asks engineering to assess and respond to the following:

*1. HGX B300 Enablement*
 * Can RHOSO support HGX B300 GPU passthrough with Fabric Manager as a host-local integration?

 * Are additional Nova, Placement, or Cyborg changes required?

 * Is NVLink currently treated as a single PCI group, and if so, what work is required to support NVLink partitioning/isolation between VMs?

*2. NVLink Multi-Tenancy Model*
 * What options exist (or are feasible) to prevent full NVLink coherence across VMs?
 ** PCI grouping changes?
 ** Fabric Manager policy integration?
 ** Explicit constraints / documented limitations?

 * What is achievable without large upstream changes vs what requires upstream Nova/Cyborg design work?

*3. RTX PRO 6000*
 * Confirmation of supported PCI passthrough workflows

*Initiative Overview (mandatory -* _Complete while in_ *_New_* _status)_
This initiative is bringing evaluation of Red Hat OpenStack (RHOSO) as the virtualization platform for NVIDIA GPU-based AI services on specific set of hardware.

There are two sets for HW to verify support, which are HGX B300 platforms and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, with specific expectations around VM-level GPU assignment and multi-tenancy.

 

*Goals (mandatory -* _Complete while in_ *_New_* _status)_
The goal is to validate below HW and specific functionality support in RHOSO with such HW

*1. NVIDIA HGX B300 (Blackwell, NVLink-based)*
 * 8-GPU NVLink/NVSwitch-based platform
 * Fabric Manager required
 * Single-node focus (no multi-node GPU pooling

Features support to validate:
 * Ability to assign GPUs to VMs
 * Support *GPU passthrough* on HGX B300 systems
 * NVIDIA Fabric Manager integration on compute hosts
 * *Critical Requirement: NVLink multi-tenancy*
 ** NVLink connectivity must be {*}partitioned between VMs{*}, so that:
 ** GPUs assigned to different VMs are not fully NVLink-coherent
 ** One VM does not gain implicit access to GPUs assigned to another VM
 

*2. NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe)*
 * Discrete PCIe GPU
 * Standard enterprise virtualization use cases

Features to validate:
 * GPU assignment to VMs via PCI passthrough
 * vGPU support (time-sliced or mediated device)
 * Live migration is not a hard requirement for initial deployment

h3. *Key Questions for Engineering*

This RFE explicitly asks engineering to assess and respond to the following:

*1. HGX B300 Enablement*
 * Can RHOSO support HGX B300 GPU passthrough with Fabric Manager as a host-local integration?

 * Are additional Nova, Placement, or Cyborg changes required?

 * Is NVLink currently treated as a single PCI group, and if so, what work is required to support NVLink partitioning/isolation between VMs?

*2. NVLink Multi-Tenancy Model*
 * What options exist (or are feasible) to prevent full NVLink coherence across VMs?
 ** PCI grouping changes?
 ** Fabric Manager policy integration?
 ** Explicit constraints / documented limitations?

 * What is achievable without large upstream changes vs what requires upstream Nova/Cyborg design work?

*3. RTX PRO 6000*
 * Confirmation of supported PCI passthrough workflows

 * Assessment of vGPU feasibility and dependencies (mdev, SR-IOV, driver constraints)

h2. Feature Request Overview (mandatory - Complete while in New status)

*What user goal or problem do you need to solve?*

In Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift 18 deployments with custom Keystone endpoint configurations, the Octavia Operator currently hardcodes authentication to use the internal Keystone endpoint. This prevents successful Octavia installation when the internal endpoint is not available or when the deployment architecture requires using a custom/external Keystone endpoint.

The Octavia Operator needs the ability to specify custom authentication credentials and endpoint configurations to support diverse deployment architectures where the standard internal endpoint is not used.
----
h2. Business justification (mandatory - Complete while in New status)

*How would this feature benefit the customer?*

This feature would enable customers to deploy Octavia in OpenStack environments with custom endpoint configurations, which is critical for:
 # {*}Deployment Flexibility{*}: Customers with specific network architectures or security requirements that mandate custom Keystone endpoints can successfully deploy Octavia without workarounds
 # {*}Production Readiness{*}: Eliminates a blocking issue preventing load-balancing-as-a-service capabilities in production environments with non-standard configurations
 # {*}Security Compliance{*}: Allows customers to maintain their required security posture by using designated authentication endpoints rather than being forced to expose internal endpoints
 # {*}Architectural Consistency{*}: Enables consistent endpoint management across all OpenStack services rather than requiring special cases for Octavia
 # {*}Reduced Support Burden{*}: Eliminates the need for complex workarounds or manual interventions during deployment

Without this feature, customers cannot utilize Octavia's load balancing capabilities in deployments where custom Keystone endpoints are required, forcing them to either compromise their architecture or forgo load balancing services entirely.
----
h2. Functional requirements (mandatory - Complete while in New status)

*What do you want the result of this feature to be? Add as many requirements as needed.*
 * *FR1: Custom Authentication Secret Support* - The Octavia Operator must support configuration of a custom Kubernetes secret containing authentication credentials (username, password, project, domain) that override the default internal endpoint credentials
 * *FR2: Custom Keystone Endpoint Configuration* - The Octavia Operator must allow specification of a custom Keystone authentication endpoint URL through the Octavia CR (Custom Resource) or operator configuration
 * *FR3: Backward Compatibility* - The implementation must maintain backward compatibility with existing deployments using internal endpoints; when no custom authentication is specified, the operator should default to current behavior
 * *FR4: Validation and Error Reporting* - The operator must validate custom authentication credentials and endpoints during reconciliation and provide clear error messages if authentication fails, including which endpoint was attempted
 * *FR5: Documentation* - Comprehensive documentation must be provided showing how to configure custom authentication secrets and endpoints for the Octavia Operator, including examples for common use cases
 * *FR6: Secret Reference in Octavia CR* - Add a new field in the Octavia CR spec (e.g., {{{}keystoneAuthSecretRef{}}}) that allows referencing a custom secret for authentication rather than using the default secret
 * *FR7: Endpoint Override Configuration* - Add configuration options in the Octavia CR to specify custom endpoints for Keystone authentication (e.g., {{{}keystoneAuthURL{}}})

----
h2. Describe the customer impact

*IMPORTANT: Do not include customer names.*
 * {*}Provide links to the account project{*}: [Add your account project link here if available]
 * {*}Provide links to any related support tickets (open or closed){*}:
 ** [https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/04285608] - Original support case documenting the authentication failure and recommendation to open this RFE
 * {*}Current Impact{*}:
 ** Customer is blocked from deploying Octavia in their Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift 18 environment
 ** Error: "error while setting the compute quotas: Authentication failed" during Octavia operator reconciliation
 ** Root cause: Operator attempts to authenticate against internal Keystone endpoint which is unavailable in their deployment architecture
 ** Customer requires custom Keystone endpoint for their production environment due to network architecture requirements
 * {*}Workaround Status{*}: No viable workaround currently exists that maintains the customer's required architecture

----

*Provide any additional points of contact for this feature request, such as an account executive, SA, or TAM:*
 * [Add SA/TAM name and contact if applicable]
 * [Add Account Executive if applicable]

----

[Use More > Link to add related issues such as:]
 * Link to original support case: [https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/04285608]
 * Any related documentation or architecture diagrams that illustrate the custom endpoint requirement

----
This RFE provides a comprehensive case for adding flexible authentication configuration to the Octavia Operator while maintaining backward compatibility with existing deployments.

h2. Feature Overview

* How much can we upstream into leapp so that the RHEL upgrade is 'normal' with no special caveats?
* What do we need to do to get our packages/repositories into the leapp repomap, etc?
* Wrap or don't wrap leapp in edpm-ansible playbooks.
* If we do, we should collaborate with RHEL rather than roll our own. See [RHELBU-3269|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHELBU-3269] Create a System Role for Upgrades (scheduled for release in RHEL 9.8 GA)
* Cater for any EDPM host, including Networker, Storage (Ceph/Swift), Compute
* How do we feel about allowing customers to co-ordinate system upgrades via external tools (Satellite, AAP, gitlab, jenkins), rather than forcing our own methods?
* TODO: need feedback from PM about UX and requirements
* Ansible roles compatibility in RHEL9 and RHEL10 (different versions of ansible, python, libs)

h2. Goals

h3. 1. Data Plane OS Upgrade Readiness

Develop and validate the upgrade path for RHOSO data plane nodes from RHEL 9.6 to RHEL 10.2, ensuring compute, network, and storage services remain functional.

* Identify and resolve package dependency changes between RHEL 9.6 and 10.2
* Address Python 3.9 → 3.12 migration impact on ansible roles and custom scripts running on data plane nodes without containers
* Document any deprecated/removed packages and their replacements

h3. 2. Upgrade Automation & EDPM Ansible Playbook Development

Design and implement EDPM Ansible-based automation for the RHEL 9.6(8/10) → 10.2(4) data plane in place upgrade (leapp).

* Develop/update EDPM-ansible roles to support RHEL 10.2(4) targets
* Ensure the role can handle pre-upgrade validation, upgrade process, and post-upgrade health checks
* Achieve upgrade automation coverage for all supported data plane node roles (compute, networker, storage)

h3. 3. Python 3.12 Migration

Ensure all non-containerised OpenStack components and dependencies on data plane nodes are fully compatible with Python 3.12 (RHEL 10.2 default). Ensure EDPM-Ansible roles and modules are fully compatible with Python 3.12.

* Audit custom scripts, plugins, and integrations for Python 3.9 → 3.12 breaking changes
* Test and validate all OpenStack client libraries and agents against Python 3.12
* Test and validate edpm-ansible roles and modules are fully compatible with Python 3.12

h3. 4. Compatibility & Integration Testing

Build and execute a comprehensive test plan covering RHOSO 19 control plane and RHEL 10.2 data plane integration.

* Test driver/kernel compatibility (DPDK, SR-IOV, GPU passthrough) on RHEL 10.2
* Validate live migration between RHEL 9.6 and RHEL 10.2 compute nodes during rolling upgrades

h3. 5. Upgrade Documentation & Runbooks

Produce upgrade documentation and operational runbooks for the RHOSO 18 → 19 RHEL transition.

* Document supported upgrade paths
* Publish known issues and workarounds

h3. 6. Performance & Scalability Validation

Benchmark RHOSO 19 on RHEL 10.2 against RHOSO 18 on RHEL 9.6 baselines to ensure no performance regressions.

* Measure VM provisioning speed, network throughput, and storage IOPS post-upgrade
* Validate at-scale deployment (target: N compute nodes) meets existing SLAs
* Report and resolve any regressions before GA

h3. 7. Customer/Stakeholder Enablement

Enable downstream teams and customers to plan and execute the upgrade confidently.

* Deliver internal knowledge transfer sessions on upgrade architecture and procedures
* Contribute to release notes and upgrade guide content
* Support early adopter/beta customer upgrades and incorporate feedback

Goal: Ensure all non containerised OpenStack components and dependencies on data plane nodes are fully compatible with Python 3.12 (RHEL 10.2 default). Ensure EDPM-Ansible roles and modules are fully compatible with Python 3.12

Goal: Build and execute a comprehensive test plan covering RHOSO 19 control plane and RHEL 10.2 data plane integration.

* Test driver/kernel compatibility (DPDK, SR-IOV, GPU passthrough) on RHEL 10.2
* Validate live migration between RHEL 9.6 and RHEL 10.2 compute nodes during rolling upgrades.

h2. 5. Upgrade Documentation & Runbooks

Goal: Produce upgrade documentation and operational runbooks for the RHOSO 18 → 19 RHEL transition.

* Document supported upgrade paths
* Publish known issues and workarounds

h2. 6. Performance & Scalability Validation

Goal: Benchmark RHOSO 19 on RHEL 10.2 against RHOSO 18 on RHEL 9.6 baselines to ensure no performance regressions.

* Measure VM provisioning speed, network throughput, and storage IOPS post-upgrade
* Validate at-scale deployment (target: N compute nodes) meets existing SLAs
* Report and resolve any regressions before GA

h2. 7. Customer/Stakeholder Enablement

Goal: Enable downstream teams and customers to plan and execute the upgrade confidently.

* Deliver internal knowledge transfer sessions on upgrade architecture and procedures
* Contribute to release notes and upgrade guide content
* Support early adopter/beta customer upgrades and incorporate feedback
